transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, I came in because I just feel... wound up almost all day. It's like my body is constantly bracing for something. Even when I'm just sitting at my computer working, or trying to relax after dinner, I just have this tense feeling that I can't really seem to shake.
Do you ever have sudden surges of intense fear or discomfort that peak within minutes?

No, I wouldn't say I get anything like that. It's not really a sudden rush of fear or anything... it's just that steady, low-level tension I mentioned. I haven't had any intense peaks like you're describing.
Did this constant tension start after a particularly stressful event happened in your life?

Yes, I suppose it did. Um, this has been going on for about thirteen months now. That was right around the time my sister in Arecibo started needing a lot more help from the family... so, yeah, I'd say that's when it all started.
Do you find that the worrying feels hard to control?

Yeah, I do. I try to stop it... I’ll tell myself, Daniela, enough, just focus on this report. But it doesn't really work. One small thought just turns into five more, and before I know it, I’ve spent half an hour checking messages or just replaying what could go wrong instead of doing my work. It's definitely hard to rein in.
Do you find yourself worrying about many different parts of your life, rather than mainly about your sister's situation?

Yes, it's definitely not just about my sister. My mind kind of... well, it just keeps going from one concern to another. I'll be thinking about her down in Arecibo, and then suddenly I'm worrying about whether I missed something on a project at the office, or if my husband is safe driving home. Then it's on to church commitments, or the bills. It's like I always find myself preparing for problems that haven’t even happened yet.
Has this excessive worrying been present more days than not for at least the past six months?
Yes, definitely. Like I mentioned earlier, it's been going on for about thirteen months now, and it's pretty much an everyday thing. There are very few days where I don't feel this way.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?

Yes, I do. Actually, that's a big part of why I came in. I just feel wound up almost all day long. It's like my body is constantly bracing for something to happen. Even when I'm just sitting at my computer working, or trying to relax at home after dinner, I still have that on-edge feeling.
Do you get tired easily because of this constant worrying and tension?

No, not really. I mean, I feel wound up and tense, like I said, but it doesn't really make me feel physically tired or exhausted. I still have the energy to get through my day and do what I need to do.
Do you have trouble concentrating because your mind goes blank or gets pulled into worry?

No, I haven't really noticed that happening. I mean, I'm definitely worrying, but it doesn't seem to mess with my focus. My mind doesn't go blank or anything like that... I can still concentrate on my work at the computer just fine.
Do you find yourself getting unusually irritable?

Yes, I have noticed that. I'm usually a pretty patient person, but lately, little things are just getting under my skin. Like... if there's a late update in a documentation meeting at work, or even if someone is singing off-tempo at my choir practice. Or just getting asked too many questions while I'm cooking on a Sunday. I just find myself answering a lot sharper than I really mean to.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yes, I have. Most nights I do fall asleep eventually, but... I end up waking up around three or four in the morning. My mind just starts going over things, like my sister’s next appointment or some server issue at work. And the frustrating part is, even when I technically get enough hours of sleep, I start the morning feeling like I never really rested at all.
Even though this started when your sister needed more help, does your anxiety now feel out of proportion to what most people would feel in that situation?

I don't really think so. I mean... it feels pretty understandable to me. Juggling her needs with my job is just a lot to handle right now. I feel like most people would probably be just as worried if they were in my shoes.
When there isn’t anything urgent happening with your sister or other responsibilities, do you still feel anxious?

Yes, I do. It just seems like... my mind keeps going from one concern right to another. Even if there's no immediate emergency, I'll be thinking about my sister down in Arecibo, and then I'm suddenly wondering whether I missed something important at the office. 

Then it just shifts to other things, like my husband driving home, or my church commitments, or the bills. I just find myself constantly preparing for problems that haven’t even happened yet.
Has this worrying been interfering with your daily life?

I mean, I'm still getting my work done, and I'm showing up for my family and church commitments. But... yes, it does interfere a bit. It takes me longer to finish my reports at the office because I just find myself double-checking things way more than I used to. And... well, I've had to apologize a few times lately for sounding short with the people I care about. The worrying just kind of wears on my patience, I guess.
Would you say your anxiety is mainly centered on dealing with your sister’s situation?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean... it definitely started with her, but now it's not really focused on just one thing. Like I mentioned, it just kind of bounces around from her, to my job, to my husband. It's really just a mix of everything at this point.
